headline: 21,988 river grabbers identified across 64 districts
summary: Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam informed parliament that the National River Protection Commission has updated the list of illegal occupiers nationwide.
details: Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam told parliament that at least 21,988 illegal occupiers of the country's rivers have been identified nationwide.
The National River Protection Commission updated the list of illegal occupiers on December 23, 2025.
Deputy commissioners have been asked to verify the list and submit eviction plans to facilitate upcoming eviction drives.
According to the official list published on April 14, 2025, Bangladesh has a total of 1,415 rivers.
This comprehensive list was prepared with the assistance of multiple agencies, including divisional commissioners, district administrations, and river workers.

headline: Narsingdi: Man arrested for throwing dog into river with brick tied to neck
summary: Police detained the suspect after a video of the animal cruelty incident went viral on social media.
details: Police in Narsingdi have arrested a 25-year-old man for allegedly tying a brick to a dog's neck and throwing it into the Meghna River.
The suspect, identified as Mohammad Ali, was detained from his home yesterday following the circulation of a viral video on Facebook.
The footage shows a man tying a rope around a dog's neck, attaching a brick to the other end, and throwing the animal from Nagariakandi Bridge.
The incident reportedly took place on June 24. Narsingdi Sadar Model Police Station OC ARM Mamun confirmed the arrest.
Authorities identified the suspect through the online footage. The current condition and fate of the dog could not be immediately confirmed.
